questions: Should the heatmap have annotations (annot=True) as in the reference solution, or is that an implementation detail left unspecified?
Is the correlation matrix computed using the default method (Pearson) or should another method (e.g., Spearman) be used?
Should the function close any matplotlib figures or leave them open for the caller?
If the input contains non-numeric data, should the function raise a ValueError (as implied by test) or let pandas/seaborn raise their own exceptions?
Should the heatmap be returned as a matplotlib Axes object (sns.heatmap return) or as a figure?
Are the column names always exactly 'A' through 'E' in that order, or could they be assigned based on sublist order if length matches?
Should the function set any specific styling for the heatmap (e.g., colormap, figure size, title)?
If the input has exactly one row (single sublist), correlation matrix is undefined (NaN). Should the function still return a heatmap with NaN values or handle this case differently?
